verifications.claim: Gold prices have recently declined from record highs.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'gold plunging to $4,691.70 per ounce (-4.18%) ... gold surged above $5,600'; R2: 'Spot gold slid more than 3% to $4,654.29'; R4: 'gold falling about 7% ... peaks earlier this year, gold prices rose about $5,600'; R9: 'decline of roughly 13% from its latest record high [$5,589.38]'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state recent declines from record highs with specific prices and percentages.

verifications.claim: Investors are favoring the dollar over gold amidst geopolitical tension, say The Economic Times.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1 (Economic Times): 'investors are choosing the dollar and oil over gold and silver. That shift in preference is critical ... Even though geopolitical uncertainty remains high'
verifications.reasoning: R1 (ET) directly supports favoring dollar over gold during US-Iran war tensions.

verifications.claim: Robust oil prices have fueled inflation fears that diminish the appeal of non-yielding bullion, say The Economic Times.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1 (Economic Times): 'Rising energy prices are fueling inflation fears globally ... makes interest-bearing assets more attractive compared to gold and silver, which do not offer any yield'
verifications.reasoning: R1 (ET) explicitly links oil/energy prices to inflation fears reducing appeal of non-yielding gold/silver.

verifications.claim: The U.S. dollar has rebounded, causing an inverse effect on gold prices, as highlighted in this YouTube video.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'strength of the U.S. dollar ... A stronger dollar often leads to weaker metals prices'; R2: 'further strengthening in the U.S. dollar. Gold often declines when the U.S. dollar appreciates'; R4: 'dollar has also strengthened ... inverse correlation with metals prices'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe dollar rebound/strength causing inverse pressure on gold; no YouTube but fact faithfully represented.

verifications.claim: Investors are adjusting expectations to believe the Federal Reserve will maintain higher interest rates for longer, note The Economic Times.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1 (Economic Times): 'expectations of Federal Reserve rate cuts are fading fast ... markets begin to price out interest rate cuts ... delaying the very rate cuts'
verifications.reasoning: R1 (ET) clearly states fading rate cut expectations, implying higher rates for longer.

verifications.claim: Investors have currently turned to the U.S. dollar as their primary safe-haven asset, say this YouTube video.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'investors are choosing the dollar and oil over gold and silver'; R2: 'investors search for the quickest assets to sell ... perceived safe haven assets are sold'
verifications.reasoning: Sources support shift to dollar as safe-haven over gold; no YouTube but fact supported.

verifications.claim: Rising energy and oil prices are driving concerns about persistent inflation.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Rising energy prices are fueling inflation fears'; R2: 'fears about the Iran war and inflation ... energy shock that will add inflationary pressure'; R4: 'Surging oil prices amid the Iran war and inflationary fears'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly link rising oil/energy prices to inflation concerns.

verifications.claim: Forbes and CNBC reported downward pressure on gold.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2 (CNBC): 'Gold and silver joined a broad sell-off ... Spot gold slid more than 3%'; R4 (Forbes): 'Gold and silver faced a steep selloff ... gold falling about 7%'
verifications.reasoning: R2 (CNBC) and R4 (Forbes) directly report gold price declines and sell-offs.

verifications.claim: Gold prices hit all-time highs earlier in 2026, as explained in this CBS News article.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R9 (CBS News): 'reaching $5,589.38 per ounce in late January — its highest point ever'
verifications.reasoning: R9 (CBS) explicitly states all-time high in early 2026.
